title: E. Eduardo Looking for Juan (Hard Version)

legend: This is the hard version of the problem. The difference is that L%%ZSMJ0%% will be in the input.

Eduardo has been looking for Juan for a long time, he finally found out that Juan is on some mountain The Horse Land but before he heads looking for him there he asked Ahmad for help, but he is too busy so it's your responsibility to help him.
Eduardo knows that The Horse Land is n%%ZSMJ1%% lands connected by n−1%%ZSMJ2%% roads and there is a unique path between every two lands.

Furthermore, each land has a height ai%%ZSMJ3%%, Eduardo will travel from u%%ZSMJ4%% to v%%ZSMJ5%%, but he can only do that if the multiplication of the height of the nodes on the way is a perfect square.
In a formal way let p1,...,pk%%ZSMJ6%% the lands in the simple path from u%%ZSMJ7%% to v%%ZSMJ8%%, where p1=u%%ZSMJ9%% and pk=v%%ZSMJ10%%, ∏ki=1api%%ZSMJ11%% should be a perfect square.
Eduardo hates surprises, so he will ask you about q%%ZSMJ12%% scenarios:

u%%ZSMJ13%% v%%ZSMJ14%%: what is the minimum number of operations so that the multiplication on the simple path from u%%ZSMJ15%% to v%%ZSMJ16%% is a perfect square? In one operation, you can choose a land i%%ZSMJ17%% and multiply its height by some number 1≤x≤L%%ZSMJ18%%.
input: The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ19%% (2≤n≤106)%%ZSMJ20%% and L%%ZSMJ21%% (70≤L≤104)%%ZSMJ22%% – the number of lands and the limit for x%%ZSMJ23%%.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ24%% integers (1≤ai≤70)%%ZSMJ25%% – the heights of the lands.

The next n−1%%ZSMJ26%% lines describes the roads, the ith%%ZSMJ27%% line contains two integers u%%ZSMJ28%% v%%ZSMJ29%% meaning there is a two-way road between u%%ZSMJ30%% and v%%ZSMJ31%% (1≤u,v≤n)%%ZSMJ32%%.
The next line contains a single integer q%%ZSMJ33%% (1≤q≤5×105)%%ZSMJ34%% – the number scenarios.
The next q%%ZSMJ35%% lines each contains two integers u%%ZSMJ36%% v%%ZSMJ37%% (1≤u,v≤n)%%ZSMJ38%%.
output: Print q%%ZSMJ39%% lines, each line is the answer to the ith%%ZSMJ40%% scenario.
